summary: This joint resolution nullifies the EPA rule published April 6, 2023, that grants California a preemption waiver for its heavy-duty vehicle emission standards, warranty rules, and zero-emission requirements.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving an EPA emissions rule. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation addresses vehicle emissions standards only and has no connection to healthcare policy or systems.
No references to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill is silent on immigration, borders, or related enforcement.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy elements.

The joint resolution uses the CRA to nullify an EPA rule that had approved California's stricter heavy-duty vehicle emissions standards, including Advanced Clean Trucks and zero-emission requirements. By repealing these standards, the bill directly limits environmental regulations on vehicle pollution.
No provisions concerning welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety-net benefits.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policy content.
No criminal sentencing, policing, or justice reform measures.
The legislation does not involve tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy language.
No provisions touching on LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains nothing about foreign assistance or international aid.
No election administration, voting access, or electoral integrity measures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight content.
The resolution does not address labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
No religious liberty, civil rights, or anti-discrimination provisions.
